answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake for a long horizon before it can earn reputation-weighted work. Rewards accrue only after counterparties complete repeated tasks, while proven fraud burns the stake and resets reputation. A public cipher can bind each task receipt to the same locked key, making copied credentials detectable without treating a key as proof of a unique human. To forge influence, an attacker must fund many independent stakes and keep them locked through the earning period, tying up capital that can be slashed.
